W5-BEH-WSL-SUITE.reason: One test failed: tests/test_app_smoke.py::test_hide_menu_and_reload, whose app menu had a 'Recent messages' entry it doesn't expect (a bubble shown before the test hid the chatmon). The first run failed six others instead (W5-BEH-WSL-SUITE-LOADED). Each passed alone (wave5/suite-linux-failures-rerun.log, 6 of 6), and tests/test_app_smoke.py passed five runs in five on its own (wave5/smoke-wsl-5-runs.log, 97 passed each). In main's CI run 43778643147 the two smoke tests passed on all twelve test legs (and in the distro drill's two green runs), and the sway click test in the sway job; the compositor checks skip in CI, where KWin and Hyprland aren't installed. So the whole WSL suite has timing-sensitive smoke and compositor tests that fail now and then on WSL's /mnt/c tree; none is M3 behaviour, and M3's criteria are carried by W5-BEH-WSL-M3, W5-BEH-WSL-SWAY, the Windows suite, CI and the drills, which all pass. Next: the coordinator may make those tests' waits robust on a slow tree (reported, not changed here); then the whole WSL suite runs again.

With nothing showing, 5 s on, the overlay held 2 640x640 buffers (3.1 MB) and drew 7 frames in 2 s; that is within M3-04's at most two buffers sized to what is shown. The fb19cb9 side of the comparison is M3's own memory-before--window.json, whose code (revision 2's) hasn't changed.
